title: Email and follow-ups
point: Open, chase, ask and sign off the way people write work emails and messages: short, direct and polite.

sentences.ja: 返信が遅くなってすみません。
sentences.note: In a more formal email, "Apologies for the delay" does the same job.

sentences.ja: 先日お送りしたメールの件で、確認のご連絡です。
sentences.text: I'm just following up on my last email.
sentences.note: "Just following up" is the polite, standard way to chase a reply.
"Please find attached" is older and more formal; most people now write "I've attached".

sentences.ja: ご不明な点があれば、お気軽にご連絡ください。
sentences.text: Let me know if you have any questions.
sentences.note: This line closes most work emails; "Feel free to reach out" is a slightly warmer version.

sentences.ja: ご返信ありがとうございます。
sentences.text: Thanks for getting back to me.
sentences.note: Use this when someone replies to you; "Thanks for reaching out" fits when they contact you first.

sentences.ja: 金曜日までにお返事いただけると助かります。
sentences.text: It would be great if you could get back to me by Friday.
sentences.note: "It would be great if you could…" sets a deadline without sounding pushy.

sentences.ja: 念のため確認ですが、会議は明日の2時からのままですか？
sentences.text: Just to double-check, is the meeting still at two tomorrow?

sentences.ja: このメールを担当者に転送しておきます。
sentences.text: I'll forward this to the right person.
sentences.note: "The person in charge" is fine too; "the right person" sounds less formal.

sentences.ja: サラさんもCCに入れておきますね。
sentences.note: "Cc" works as a verb: you cc someone on an email.

sentences.ja: これから一緒にお仕事できるのを楽しみにしています。よろしくお願いします。
sentences.text: Looking forward to working with you.
sentences.note: English has no single よろしくお願いします; pick the line that fits, such as this, "Thanks in advance" or just "Best".
